subject: general
question: Sapna invested ₹20,000 on simple interest, partly at 12% per annum and partly at 13% per annum. If she earns equal interests from the two investments after 7 years, then find the sum invested at 12% per annum (in ₹).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When Simple Interest is equal for the same time period, principal amounts are inversely proportional to their respective interest rates.

Ratio of investments = P₁ : P₂ = R₂ : R₁ = 13 : 12

Total ratio parts = 13 + 12 = 25 parts

Value of 25 parts = ₹20,000 ⇒ 1 part = ₹800

Sum invested at 12% (P₁) = 13 parts × 800 = ₹10,400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10,400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Principal (P) = ₹20,000

Rate 1 (R₁) = 12%, Rate 2 (R₂) = 13%

Time (T) = 7 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100
